request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 37.2% (95% band 23.0% to 56.2%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.6; >= 2: +2.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.70, 95% band [+2.30, +2.87]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 19.8% (95% band 12.5% to 24.8%); rank 2 to 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 149999: +0.3; >= 150000: -0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.87, 95% band [-1.31, -0.49]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 10.7% (95% band 3.9% to 17.7%); rank 2 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.51 (95% band [-1.02, -0.09]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 18,100 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 4.6% (95% band 0.0% to 9.5%); rank 3 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.16, 95% band [-0.37, +0.20]).
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 4.4% (95% band 0.2% to 5.1%); rank 4 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.41, 95% band [-0.03, +0.60]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 3.7% (95% band 0.3% to 7.0%); rank 4 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.19, 95% band [-0.41, +0.40]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 3.0% (95% band 0.3% to 10.2%); rank 3 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.23, 95% band [+0.00, +1.12]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.0% to 6.4%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.10, 95% band [-0.22, +0.58]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 0.1% (95% band 0.0% to 1.7%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.00, 95% band [-0.01, +0.10]).

Interactions: the model has 26 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 2.2% (95% band 0.9% to 4.7%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.60 (95% band +2.17 to +2.82) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +2.66 (95% band +1.84 to +3.03) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 450,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 450,000: -0.92 (95% band -1.34 to -0.51) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.86 (95% band -1.66 to -0.27) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.0% to 2.7%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 450,000: -0.92 (95% band -1.34 to -0.49) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -0.79 (95% band -1.37 to -0.48) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,100: -0.53 (95% band -1.01 to -0.05) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.40 (95% band -0.97 to +0.11) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 450,000.
- `PAY_0 & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.0% to 2.9%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.54 (95% band +1.78 to +2.85) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +2.75 (95% band +2.31 to +2.94) when `BILL_AMT1` = 203,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 203,000: +0.12 (95% band -0.43 to +0.21) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.33 (95% band -0.30 to +0.79) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.0%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 450,000: -0.98 (95% band -1.46 to -0.49) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.78 (95% band -1.23 to -0.49) when `BILL_AMT1` = 203,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 203,000: +0.03 (95% band -0.48 to +0.40) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.23 (95% band -0.30 to +0.43) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 450,000.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 3.1%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.64 (95% band +2.22 to +2.83) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, +2.74 (95% band +2.04 to +2.93) when `PAY_AMT3` = 17,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 17,000: -0.18 (95% band -0.40 to +0.23) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.08 (95% band -0.63 to +0.33) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & AGE`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 2.0%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 450,000: -0.86 (95% band -1.21 to -0.46) when `AGE` = 23, -0.85 (95% band -1.40 to -0.45) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.47 (95% band +0.00 to +0.68) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.47 (95% band -0.14 to +0.53) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 450,000.
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 2.1%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 203,000: +0.23 (95% band -0.25 to +0.53) when `AGE` = 23, +0.08 (95% band -0.45 to +0.29) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.46 (95% band -0.00 to +0.50) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +0.31 (95% band -0.31 to +0.44) when `BILL_AMT1` = 203,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 450,000: -0.94 (95% band -1.40 to -0.49) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -0.94 (95% band -1.24 to -0.49) when `PAY_AMT2` = 18,300.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 18,300: +0.10 (95% band -0.27 to +0.61) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.10 (95% band -0.23 to +0.70) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 450,000.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.2% to 2.8%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.64 (95% band +2.26 to +2.94) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +2.87 (95% band +2.32 to +3.14) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,100: -0.52 (95% band -1.08 to -0.09) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.29 (95% band -0.77 to -0.02) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_AMT1 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,100: -0.54 (95% band -1.01 to -0.12) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -0.43 (95% band -0.99 to -0.09) when `PAY_AMT2` = 18,300.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 18,300: +0.04 (95% band -0.22 to +0.48) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.16 (95% band -0.22 to +0.74) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,100.
- `PAY_0 & AGE`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 2.8%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.71 (95% band +2.23 to +2.90) when `AGE` = 23, +2.71 (95% band +2.33 to +3.06) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.41 (95% band -0.06 to +0.59) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.40 (95% band -0.05 to +0.75) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 203,000: +0.16 (95% band -0.43 to +0.42) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.22 (95% band -0.42 to +0.40) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,100.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by the most recent repayment status, PAY_0: applicants who were already at least two months late in September 2005 carry a much higher predicted risk, about 2.3 log-odds units above those paid in full, and this accounts for roughly 37% of the model's importance."},{"id":2,"text":"The credit limit, LIMIT_BAL, is the second main driver (about 20% of importance): applicants with limits of 150,000 NT dollars or more get a lower predicted risk than those below that level, with the net effect across the middle of the data spanning roughly -0.9 log-odds units."},{"id":3,"text":"The amount paid in September 2005, PAY_AMT1, matters less (about 11% of importance): larger payments are associated with lower predicted risk, a shift of about -0.5 log-odds units from the lowest to the highest typical payments, though the shape between those points is not resolved by the data."},{"id":4,"text":"The effect of PAY_0 is broadly similar regardless of credit limit, age, or bill amount, so the interactions involving it are small in practice; the data do not settle whether the lower risk from higher limits or larger payments differs much between applicants who are current and those who are late."},{"id":5,"text":"Several other variables, including the older payment amounts, bill statement amounts, age, and education, have importance shares of 5% or less and effects whose bands include zero, so the data do not show that they reliably move predictions."},{"id":6,"text":"Overall, the model's predictions rest on recent payment behaviour, followed by the size of the credit limit and the latest payment, and the remaining interactions are too small or too uncertain to interpret with confidence."}]}
